notes.summary: ROOT310 independently reconstructed: one actual shared face can be synchronized with whole-cell supports and rational spatial REAL-PA carriers. Compatibility on other faces is not preserved automatically.
notes.detailedSummary: The closed epigraph construction has proper rational projection domains, attained finite fibers, rational lower graph carriers despite real heights, and exact whole-face restrictions. Exposure inside each original cell and an explicit zero-ray recession inclusion establish the correction. Common supports hold at every real face point on entire incident cells. Bounded growth, recession and unshifted contacts survive. This is a single-face result, not general regularity.
notes.text:
Let nonempty closed rational cells sigma_i share a nonempty actual face tau. Let finite continuous convex f_i agree there, and assume that at every y in tau one ambient covector supports all f_i on their ENTIRE sigma_i. Suppose convex rational-spatial REAL-PA roofs satisfy f_i<=P_i<=f_i+eta.

Finite polyhedral facts used in the construction can be proved directly. Remove a cone's rational lineality, including both signed basis directions in its generators. In the pointed quotient the sum of nonnegative defining rows is positive away from zero. Its section of value one is bounded, since normalization of an unbounded sequence would produce a nonzero cone vector of value zero. A bounded polyhedron is generated by finitely many vertices: move at a nonvertex in both signs of a direction annihilating its active rows until new independent rows become active, then induct on active rank. Rational systems give rational vertices. Homogenization gives finite point/ray generation of arbitrary nonempty polyhedra. Projection preserves polyhedrality by eliminating a variable through pairing all lower and upper bounds; missing-sided bounds and equalities cause no exception.

For E_i=conv A_i+cone R_i, closedconv(union E_i)=conv(union A_i)+cone(union R_i). The right side is a closed polyhedron containing every source. Conversely a ray sr from one source can be added to a hull point u by taking the limit of (1-delta)u+delta(a+sr/delta), where a belongs to that source. Approximate closed-hull points and add finitely many rays. Thus closure is essential, rather than assuming the ordinary union hull closed.

Set E_i=epi(P_i+I_sigma_i), K=closedconv(union E_i), and let G be its lower function. Each E_i has finite lifted generators with rational spatial coordinates and actual real heights, obtained from its rational affinity regions and the vertical ray. One common original support at a fixed tau point bounds K below. Its spatial projection D is the rational hull/cone of the spatial generators. Every nonempty vertical fiber is closed, bounded below and attains its finite minimum. In a finite inequality description, upward stability forces lower height coefficients to be nonnegative. Divide positive coefficients to obtain finitely many affine lower rows; zero coefficients describe D. Therefore G is a continuous finite affine maximum on D and an active row supplies an ambient support even on the boundary of a proper domain.

A lower graph face exposed by t-ell(x) uses exactly zero-slack point and ray generators. Its projection is injective and generated by their rational spatial coordinates; the vertical ray is excluded. Graph subfaces are also lower, by summing active rows or perturbing an exposure while preserving finitely many positive slacks and the height sign. Unique graph heights make projected intersections common faces. These projections form a finite rational carrier. Matching affine tuples on such a carrier satisfy rational homogeneous equations; Gaussian elimination gives a rational kernel basis. Clearing denominators makes each basis tuple have integral tangent slopes and rational constants. Every actual matching tuple is a finite real combination of these literal PA tuples. This proves genuine REAL-PA membership without rounding heights or assuming generic irrational-wall maxima have rational walls.

At each y in tau, its original common support gives G(y)>=f_tau(y), whereas E_i inclusion gives G(y)<=min_i P_i(y)<=f_tau(y)+eta. Let g=G|tau and T=epi(g+I_tau). Rational intersection of the graph carrier with tau supplies the carrier and lifted generators for T.

For each i form K'_i=closedconv(E_i union T). Its projection is exactly sigma_i. Both generating sets lie in the closed convex epigraph of f_i, so its attained lower Q_i satisfies f_i<=Q_i<=P_i and is continuous convex rational-spatial REAL-PA.

Expose tau INSIDE sigma_i by a rational affine a_i>=0 with zero set tau. In the finite generator representation, the zero face uses only zero points and zero rays. Zero E_i points lie in epi(P_i|tau), contained in T. For a zero E_i ray (v,h), y+tv lies in tau and g(y+tv)<=P_i(y)+th. Each affine branch of g consequently has slope at most h on v, proving (v,h) belongs to rec T from every T base point. This verifies the required recession inclusion, including signed lineality, without an unsupported inference from set inclusion. Thus the zero face is exactly T and Q_i|tau=g. If tau=sigma_i, E_i is already contained in T and the conclusion is immediate.

Since E_i and T are contained in K, K'_i is contained in K. Hence Q_i>=G, with equality on tau. An active affine support of G at ANY real y in tau therefore supports every Q_i on its entire sigma_i. Bounded errors give equal forward recession secant limits. Any initial contact P_i(y)=f_tau(y) forces g(y)=Q_i(y)=f_tau(y). Actual bounded-relative growth and unshifted contacts are retained; no MA is assigned to intermediates.

For completeness, whole original-cell supports imply PC on every carrying structure. On a segment in X, partition at finitely many original-cell intersections. Restrictions are convex as suprema of touching affine supports, and transition supports prevent downward slope jumps. The whole segment is convex. A PCC witnessed in another structure has center-to-endpoint segments in X; an original support bounds each initial derivative and convex secants extend that inequality to its endpoint. Summation cancels the covector by the barycenter equation. Thus if all pairwise top-cell intersections are exactly this one tau, the corrected functions glue to global PC REAL-PA. This narrow corollary supplies no preservation on another shared face.

Qualified S306 supplies original continuous-target supports and cell roofs only under its stated balanced, continuity, refinement and affine positive-recession hypotheses. Its mandatory qualifications remain in force. ROOT310 is reconstructed data, not a grant.

notes.summary: New balanced higher-dimensional limitation: arbitrarily accurate roofs of a fixed non-PA target never become PC after any finite sequence of the four original face corrections. Alternating corrections converge geometrically on a fixed carrier.
notes.detailedSummary: For every d=k+1>=2, five t-slabs times R^k have four distinct unbounded positive-dimensional shared faces and constant positive real balancing weights. With unchanged admitted gamma, a fixed nonlinear target and initial excess heights (0,eta,eta,0), exact updates are a<-min(a,b/2), b<-min(b,a/2). Finite updates preserve positive heights, whereas PC forces both zero. A legal rational incident midpoint witnesses loss of a previously established whole-face support. The compatible PA limit exists, so this obstructs finite repetition rather than PA density.
notes.text:
Fix k>=1, ambient E=R_t times R_z^k and lattice Z^(k+1). The five original top cells are I_i times R^k with intervals (-infinity,0], [0,1], [1,2], [2,3], [3,infinity). Retain all four actual shared faces H_j={j} times R^k, j=0,1,2,3. These unbounded k-dimensional affine faces have no nonempty proper faces. Give all top cells one arbitrary actual real weight w>0. Their inward primitive normals at each H_j are opposite e_t, so every facet is balanced. A carrying orthant refinement in z also balances opposite coordinate normals with equal inherited weights.

Keep the ACTUAL reference gamma(t,z)=max(-t,0,t-3)+sum_r |z_r|. It is literal PA, continuous and globally convex, hence PC. On bounded t-slabs its nonzero recession slopes are sum |v_z|. On the outer slabs they are -v_t+sum |v_z| or v_t+sum |v_z| with the corresponding t sign. Every nonzero carrying recession direction has strictly positive slope. No reference is replaced.

Use the fixed NON-PA target f(t,z)=max(-t,0,t-3)+sum_r sqrt(1+z_r^2). For phi(s)=sqrt(1+s^2), phi''(s)=(1+s^2)^(-3/2)>0 and 0<phi(s)-|s|=1/(phi(s)+|s|)<=1. Thus f is finite continuous globally convex, 0<f-gamma<=k, and its restriction to a varying z coordinate has strictly positive second derivative, precluding finite PA.

For any epsilon>0 construct a convex rational-carrier REAL-PA p(z) above sum phi(z_r) with error at most epsilon and exact recession sum |v_r|. In one variable choose rational R with phi(R)-R<epsilon/(2k), interpolate actual real values on a rational mesh of [-R,R] of maximal length less than epsilon/(2k), and extend with slopes -1 and 1 through its endpoints. Increasing chord slopes in [-1,1] prove convexity. One-Lipschitzness bounds chord error by mesh length. Tail error is nonnegative and increases to phi(R)-R. Sum these roofs. Rational hinge carriers give genuine finite real scalar membership; actual heights are not rounded.

Initial cell roofs are gamma_t+p(z)+h(t), with h zero on outer rays and affine on each bounded interval, with vertex heights (0,eta,eta,0), eta>0. They are convex on every entire original slab, match all whole-face traces, have the exact actual recession, and satisfy 0<=P_i-f<=epsilon+eta. The parameters may be arbitrarily small for the FIXED target.

Suppose current inner heights are a,b>0 and outer heights stay zero. The exact closed hull of two adjacent slab epigraphs has lower function equal to the one-variable hull of their graph vertices plus p(z). Convexity of p proves the lower bound for mixtures, while mixtures at the same z realize the one-variable lower height. At consecutive vertex heights u,v,w the middle lower height is min(v,(u+w)/2), obtained either from the middle vertex or the chord of the two outer vertices. Correcting each slab gives the corresponding endpoint chord plus p. Therefore processing H_1 sends a to min(a,b/2), and H_2 sends b to min(b,a/2). Other traces stay unchanged. At H_0,H_3, horizontal slope zero together with a support of p bounds both incident roofs below and their trace already equals p, so those corrections do nothing.

Every finite sequence preserves a,b>0. PC at H_1 requires the incident slopes a and b-a to be nondecreasing, hence b>=2a. PC at H_2 similarly requires a>=2b. For nonnegative heights both force a=b=0. Consequently NO finite sequence of corrections at these four original faces is PC. A violating face has a legal printed midpoint test: rational endpoints (j-r,0),(j+r,0), 0<r<1 rational, assigned to its two original slabs, with coefficients 1/2 and center (j,0). The downward slope jump makes their average strictly less than the center value.

Alternating H_1 then H_2 gives after n>=1 cycles a_n=eta*2^(1-2n), b_n=eta*2^(-2n). The first pair is eta/2,eta/4, and each further cycle divides both by four. Immediately after correcting H_1 its adjacent slopes agree; after H_2, its left slope remains a and its right slope becomes -a/2. This destroys its common ambient support at EVERY z, although its whole trace is unchanged. The legal midpoint deficit there is 3ra/4.

The uniform excess above the compatible limiting roof gamma_t+p is a_n. The rational spatial carrier remains fixed and finite throughout. The limit is PC REAL-PA and within epsilon above f; varying epsilon supplies the known complete-affine regularization of this target. This theorem limits finite independent synchronization. It does not refute original balanced PA density, claim that all simultaneous methods fail, or claim that this infinite limit loses polyhedrality.

notes.summary: New simultaneous finite certificate: linear matching, band and point/ray support rows characterize continuous PC REAL-PA existence on a prescribed rational carrier. General feasibility remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The certificate permits several distinct overlaps, dependent directions, proper cells, unbounded faces and actual real coefficients. One affine support per original face and trace carrier cell controls all real points of that region on entire incident cells. Sufficiency is direct; necessity uses qualified S306 and extends refined supports along convex original-cell segments. Feasible bands around independent roofs yield uniform global above-majorants, but no universal feasible carrier is constructed.
notes.text:
Input consists of a finite pure globally embedded rational original complex with ALL faces, strictly positive actual REAL top weights balanced everywhere, an actual admitted continuous REAL-PA PC positive-at-infinity reference gamma, local continuous REAL-PA bands A_sigma,B_sigma bounded relative to gamma, and a prescribed finite common rational carrier C refining the original cells and bands. Bounds need not match across original faces. No PC predicate is hidden in the input.

For each carrier cell c choose rational generators c=conv V_c+cone R_c, including both signs for lineality. Unknown affine formulas are q_c(x)=a_c*x+b_c, with ambient extensions allowed. Add matching equations on every rho<=c: q_c(v)=q_rho(v) for v in V_rho and a_c*r=a_rho*r for r in R_rho. Impose every relevant original-cell band on V_c and its corresponding slope bounds on R_c.

For EVERY original face tau and EVERY carrier cell rho contained in tau introduce one ambient affine unknown ell_tau,rho(x)=p*x+d. Require it equal q on V_rho and in slopes on R_rho. For EVERY original top sigma incident to tau and EVERY c contained in sigma require q_c(v)>=ell_tau,rho(v) for all V_c, and a_c*r>=p*r for all R_c. These are finitely many linear equations and inequalities with rational spatial entries and actual real band entries. Prescribed rational contacts may be added as evaluation equalities, with the same contacts included in the existence claim.

Claim: the system is feasible exactly when there exists a continuous printed-PC genuine REAL-PA q affine on C within all whole-cell bands.

Sufficiency: point/ray matching gives matching on whole intersections and therefore continuity. Point/ray inequalities give bands and lower supports on entire cells by generator representations, including unbounded directions and signed lineality. The rational matching-kernel argument in n1 gives genuine finite real scalar PA. Each ell equals q on the WHOLE rho and lies below q on every entire incident original cell. Every real y in tau belongs to some rho, so these are common supports at all points, including irrational points and boundary points. Top-face rows also cover cell interiors. The local-to-all-structures argument in n1 proves every printed PCC. Bands give q-gamma bounded.

Necessity: suppose such q exists. Continuous printed PC extends to real endpoints on original convex cells using rational perspective variables alpha_i and t_i=alpha_i*x_i. Their incidence, barycenter and endpoint constraints are rational weak linear equations/inequalities. Within the feasible minimal face, Gaussian elimination gives rational affine coordinates; rational approximations preserve inactive strict slacks and positive coefficients. Passing to limits by continuity proves ordinary convexity on each original cell.

On a common rational refinement carrying gamma affinely, qualified S306 applies: continuity, all-face balance, actual positive real weights and bounded actual reference difference are present. It gives one support on all entire incident refined cells at each y. For any x in an original cell incident to y, the initial segment y-to-x lies in an incident refined cell. The refined support bounds its initial derivative, and convex secants on the whole original cell extend that support to x. Thus the support holds on ENTIRE original cells even when gamma is affine only on the carrying refinement.

Choose y in relative interior of rho. Since q is affine on rho, testing both small tangent directions forces the support to agree with q on its entire affine hull, hence throughout rho. For a zero-dimensional rho equality at its point suffices. Its generator values satisfy all required rows. Finitely many choices furnish a feasible solution. This imports qualified S306 at its exact scope, rather than a nonlinear extension theorem.

If S306 supplies independent roofs f<=P_sigma<=f+delta, set bands P_sigma-delta<=q<=P_sigma. Feasibility implies f-delta<=q<=f+delta, so q+delta is an above-roof with error at most 2delta and unchanged actual recession. Feasible carriers for every delta_n=2^-n would give global uniform regularization; adding 4delta_n to these above-roofs gives errors in [4,6]delta_n and successive decreases at least delta_n. Shifts can lose contacts.

GENERAL FEASIBILITY is not proved. The original non-PA f lies in the bands but is not an affine tuple on the prescribed finite carrier. Infeasibility on one carrier excludes that carrier only. For arbitrary real entries this is exact mathematical linear feasibility, not an effective black-box decision oracle.

In n2 the simultaneous height constraints h0=h3=0, a,b>=0, b-2a>=0 and a-2b>=0 have unique solution a=b=0. Indeed -2(b-2a)-(a-2b)=3a<=0, and -2(a-2b)-(b-2a)=3b<=0. This finite simultaneous construction succeeds where every finite local correction schedule fails.

notes.summary: ROOT304 reconstructed and extended: balanced complete three-line products with several positive-dimensional crossings have infinite error from every finite ambient convex restriction, although their actual reference is already PA-PC.
notes.detailedSummary: Whole incident-branch supports establish printed PC with arbitrary positive real line weights. An unbounded integer midpoint family forces ambient uniform error at least 3(T-1)/4. Its distant endpoints are not a legal printed PCC. A specified crossing forces an ambient support incompatible with the nonincident line. Products retain actual balance, rational carriers and strict growth. These results limit ambient convex restriction, not original PA regularization.
notes.text:
In ambient R^2 take complete lines L0=(x,0), L1=(t,t), L2=(1-s,s). Cut at all crossings and reference breakpoints, including all intervals, rays and vertices. Their saturated primitive directions are (1,0),(1,1),(-1,1). Give each line any positive actual real weight constant along that entire line. Opposite primitive normals cancel separately at every vertex, including meetings, so there is no unbalanced boundary.

Define the ACTUAL reference branches gamma0(x)=max(-x,0,x-1), gamma1(t)=|t|, gamma2(s)=max(-4s,6s-5/2). At crossings z01=(0,0), z02=(1,0), z12=(1/2,1/2), both incident values are respectively 0,0,1/2. The extra breakpoint s=1/4 is rational. Slopes are integral, constants rational, and the reference is continuous literal PA. Negative/positive end slopes are (1,1),(1,1),(4,6), all strictly positive.

At the three crossings choose covectors (0,1), (0,-4), (-5/2,7/2). Their incident tangent slopes are respectively (0,1),(0,-4),(1,6), lying in the actual convex branch subdifferentials. Thus each supports the ENTIRE two incident branches. At nonmeeting points extend a line subgradient ambiently. The argument in n1 proves PC on every carrying structure. The third, nonincident line imposes no support constraint at a crossing.

For any integer T>=2, let a=(T,T) in L1, b=(2-2T,0) in L0, and c=(a+b)/2=(1-T/2,T/2) in L2. Exact reference values are T,2T-2,3T-5/2. If a finite convex F on ALL ambient R^2 had finite uniform restriction error e, global convex Jensen would give 3T-5/2-e<=F(c)<=(F(a)+F(b))/2<=3T/2-1+e, hence e>=3(T-1)/4 for every T. Therefore every such F has infinite error. This is an algebraic proof on the unbounded family, not a finite-grid extrapolation. The comparison is NOT a printed PCC at c: its endpoint cells are nonincident.

A finite convex function on full R^2 has an ambient subgradient everywhere. Cube-vertex upper bounds, reflection lower bounds and convex secants give local Lipschitzness and a closed epigraph. Nearest-point separating normals from (x,G(x)-delta), normalized and passed to a unit limit, give a nonzero support. Its height coefficient is negative; zero would be a nonzero purely spatial support on a full spatial domain, impossible. Division supplies the subgradient.

If a finite globally convex G<=gamma on the entire arrangement equals gamma at z12, signed secants along its differentiable L1 and L2 restrictions force every support to have tangent slopes 1 and 6. Independent directions force the unique covector (-5/2,7/2) and touching form ell(x,y)=-5x/2+7y/2. But ell(-1,0)=5/2>gamma0(-1)=1, contradicting ell<=G<=gamma. Thus no ambient convex minorant retains this crossing value.

For each k>=1 take the product of this chosen ORIGINAL complex with R^k and add sum |z_r| to the actual reference. Use a coordinate-orthant carrying refinement. Tangent lattices are the saturated line vector plus coordinate vectors; opposite line normals cancel at original crossing facets and opposite coordinate normals at refinement facets. Actual weights remain positive real. The distinct complete-page intersections are unbounded positive-dimensional actual faces of the chosen original complex; their orthant pieces are carrying faces. Product supports prove PC, and sums of end/orthant slopes prove strict growth. Restrict any finite ambient convex function to z=0 to recover the two-dimensional obstruction. Infinite error and failure of exact minorant contact therefore persist.

This reference is ITSELF literal PA-PC. For obstacle zero its actual original envelope equals it, because it is an admitted competitor and the obstacle bounds every competitor by it. No original regularization counterexample follows. ROOT304's historical counts and absent S292 reference were not imported.

notes.text:
The exact original envelope is P_gamma(u)(x)=sup{q(x): q finite printed-PC, q<=gamma+u, q<=gamma+C_q for some real C_q}. Qualified R230 identifies it with the continuous-competitor envelope for ALL u in C_b, proves continuity and gamma-||u||<=P_gamma(u)<=gamma+u, and permits arbitrary nonseparable obstacles. It does not prove PA density or feasibility of n3's simultaneous system. Replacing q by max(q,gamma-||u||) gives a dominating two-sided-bounded printed-PC competitor but is not a PA construction.

Literal integral-slope/rational-constant PA and genuine finite REAL scalar extension remain separate. Rational spatial carriers and real heights are retained; no average, rounding or replacement of the actual reference is used. A real feasible tuple is not declared literal PA. Raw printed-PC rational/irrational downward modifications can be discontinuous; that pathology does not refute regularization of continuous-obstacle envelopes.

For source normalization, the primitive divisor coefficient is sum_sigma c_sigma*a_sigma(n_sigma/delta) minus a_delta(sum_sigma c_sigma*n_sigma/delta). A common support at a face agrees tangentially with its affine gradient and leaves nonnegative inward residual slopes. Balancing cancels its affine contribution, giving the positive convex-bend sign for the explicit nonnegative-real extension. In every dimension, projection of a saturated primitive inward normal equals covol(N_sigma)/covol(N_delta) times the inward unit conormal, with zero-dimensional covolume one. A facet lattice basis plus a primitive lift is a lattice basis; parallelepiped base-times-height proves the formula. Unconverted unit normals cannot replace primitive normals. No MA, Alexandrov formula or contact theorem is needed here, and no operator is assigned to non-PA intermediates.

All essential new BMPS immediate statement/proof units were read from the frozen text using literal newline splitting with formfeeds preserved. Formal Definitions2.19–2.20 print rational weights, although catalogue prose describes real weights; the qualified actual-real extension is declared separately. Automatic continuity and the raw-PC density equivalence are not imported. BBGS is hash-bound without a new theorem application; S306's mandatory negative unit-normal, signed/zero real coefficient and EVERY-dimensional covolume qualifications remain. Its full3.15 ends LF670 and is distinct from3.12.

Qualified B225 proves that finite positive balanced globally embedded support of positive dimension is noncompact. BMPS Definition2.4 embeds the original finite space in one N_R. Compact charted spaces, bounded skeletons and toric compactifications are different domains; the source-only empty compact branch does not resolve the catalogue's broader compact higher-dimensional residual.
